name: Sahrawi Marou
description: Marou is genuinely, deliberately simple - real Sahrawi nomadic tradition cooks rice or meat in water with only salt added, letting the meat's own natural flavor carry the dish entirely, reflecting real resourcefulness in a water-scarce environment where ingredients are precious, not a recipe missing seasoning.
steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken in 2.5 cups water with the salt, 25-28 minutes, until tender - real technique adds nothing else, letting the meat's own flavor carry the broth entirely.
Remove the chicken, add the rice to the broth, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.
Serve the rice with the chicken alongside.

name: Sahrawi Beleghman
description: Beleghman, real roasted barley flour mixed with milk, butter, or ghee and shaped into balls, is a beloved Sahrawi dish for breaking the Ramadan fast, real technique toasting the barley flour first until fragrant before mixing.
steps_detailed: Toast the barley flour in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant and lightly darkened.
Mix the toasted flour with the milk, melted butter, and honey until it holds together.
Shape into small balls and serve.

name: Sahrawi Tagine
description: Tagine, a slow-cooked stew, reflects real Berber and Maghrebi influence on Sahrawi cooking, real technique building depth from cumin, paprika, and turmeric together.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the cumin, paprika, and turmeric, and cook 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the potato and carrot with 1.5 cups water, and simmer 30-35 minutes until everything is tender.

name: Sahrawi Zriga
description: Zriga, real fermented, churned milk with the butterfat separated out, is a distinctive Sahrawi dairy product, enjoyed either sweet or salty.
steps_detailed: Whisk the yogurt vigorously for several minutes to approximate real zriga's churned, slightly separated texture.
Serve sweetened with honey, or on its own for a savory, tangy version.

name: Sahrawi Couscous
description: Couscous, the real Sahrawi staple starch, reflects genuine Maghrebi influence, real technique steaming the grains for properly light, separate texture.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

ingredients.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken, carrot, and chickpeas in 1.5 cups water 25-28 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Toss the dry couscous with a little oil and water.
Steam over the simmering stew for 10 minutes, then fluff and steam again 8-10 minutes for properly light, separate grains.
Serve the stew and broth over the finished couscous.

name: Sahrawi Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting the real Atlantic coastal fishing tradition central to the Sahrawi economy.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Sahrawi Mint Tea
description: Sahrawi tea (at-tay) is genuinely central to Sahrawi culture and social life, real technique pouring from a real height to build a light foam, often served across three distinct rounds for guests.
steps_detailed: Warm the tea with the mint 5 minutes.
Stir in the sugar until dissolved.
Pour from a real height into small glasses to build a light foam - a genuine part of Sahrawi hospitality, often repeated for three rounds.
